Maintenance Report — MNT-0019-001

Asset: WELL-0019 (SW-23 Well 019, T200, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: flowline Work started: 21 Oct 2022 08:00 · Finished: 22 Oct 2022 13:00 · Well stopped for this job: 29 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Daniel Foster, Brian Coleman · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0019-0001 on 2022-10-20 Report written: 23 Oct 2022

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0019-0001 at 09:45 on 2022-10-20 found crude oil on the pad: about 11.2% of the pad area, estimated 3.0 bbl. The inspector noted: "Dark staining on pad." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 2.3 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a threaded coupling on the flowline close to the wellhead.

Root cause

Thread fatigue from pump jack vibration.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 3 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 3% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the coupling.
  2. Cut out the failed coupling and the pipe ends.
  3. Welded in new pipe and a new fitting.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 209 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 167 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 3.9 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0019-001 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.77% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0019-006

Asset: WELL-0019 (SW-23 Well 019, T200, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 23 Apr 2023 08:00 · Finished: 25 Apr 2023 20:00 · Well stopped for this job: 60 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Brian Coleman Triggered by: inspection INS-0019-0027 on 2023-04-20 Report written: 27 Apr 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that the operator found an oil puddle under the gearbox. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0019-0027 showed the wellhead at 24.4 °C with the air at 23.7 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The input shaft seal was worn and the gearbox oil level was below the sight glass.

Root cause

Seal wear, made worse by heat and a low oil level.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 5 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Drained the gearbox oil into a closed container.
  2. Replaced the input and output shaft seals.
  3. Cleaned the base and absorbed the spilled oil.
  4. Refilled with the specified gear oil to the correct level.

Summary of the fix: replaced gearbox seals and topped up oil.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 1 hour and checked both shafts for leaks: none found. The well was returned to production.

Waste

  • Used gear oil and oily pads sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0019-006 (WS-06).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0019-023

Asset: WELL-0019 (SW-23 Well 019, T200, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: wellhead Work started: 01 Nov 2025 08:00 · Finished: 05 Nov 2025 02:00 · Well stopped for this job: 90 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Brian Coleman · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0019-0157 on 2025-10-30 Report written: 07 Nov 2025

What happened

Field staff reported that fluid was weeping from the stuffing box around the polished rod. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0019-0157 showed the wellhead at 23.1 °C with the air at 20.1 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The packing rings were worn and the polished rod was lightly scored. The well stayed shut in for about 2 days longer than the repair itself because the replacement part was back-ordered from the supplier.

Root cause

Packing wear sped up by a slightly misaligned polished rod.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 3 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Closed the wellhead valves and bled off pressure.
  2. Removed the old packing.
  3. Installed new packing rings and adjusted the gland.
  4. Cleaned the wellhead area.

Summary of the fix: replaced stuffing box packing.

Testing and return to service

Checked the stuffing box with the unit running: no leak. The well was returned to production.

maintenance.report_html:
Maintenance Report — MNT-0019-025

Asset: WELL-0019 (SW-23 Well 019, T200, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: rod string Work started: 04 Jan 2026 08:00 · Finished: 05 Jan 2026 21:00 · Well stopped for this job: 37 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Megan Ward, Daniel Foster Triggered by: inspection INS-0019-0166 on 2026-01-01 Report written: 06 Jan 2026

What happened

Field staff reported that the pump jack was running but the wellhead was cold and the rod load had dropped. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0019-0166 showed the wellhead at 10.5 °C with the air at 5.9 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A dynamometer card showed no load from the downhole pump, which points to a parted rod.

Root cause

A coupling unscrewed after repeated rod buckling at the bottom of the stroke.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rod string and located the break.
  3. Recovered the lower section with an overshot fishing tool.
  4. Replaced the damaged rods.
  5. Ran the rod string back in and spaced out the pump.

Summary of the fix: fished and replaced parted rod section.

Testing and return to service

Pump test showed normal fluid delivery and the rod load returned to normal. The well was returned to production.

Labour (company crew)4,757

  • Keep the recovered rod for failure analysis.
